x: Our sealed handicap held in conjunction provided our Walking Hon. Secretary with a "First," with Bert Field second, and L. Jones, continuing in his great promise, third.

Joe King was second man home, and with Bert Field completing the team, we were placed second in the scratch team race. Both scratch and team events went to the Surrey Walking Club, who had a very fine day out, for in addition they supplied first (H.

Fifth position was filled by Bert Field, his usual consistent self, which makes him such a reliable team man. Harley, who finished sixth, fell away slightly over the last three miles, but was nearly six minutes faster than last year; R.

Bert Field completed our team a place behind Martin, and once again illustrated his extreme dependability. Our four scored 42 points, but Surrey Walking Club, the holders, had managed to retain their title by scoring 40 points.
Jessup (Valentine's S.C.) third and our two, Bert.
Immediately following our third man, Green, were "Jock" Martin and Bert Field, giving the finest support to our scoring team that it would be possible to have.

Our team this year contained only three of the eight who did duty for us last year, the absentees being such well-known walkers as Tommy Green, Fred Rickards, Jack Bidgood, Bert Field and Bill Holman.
Our next were walking in trio, Bentley 13th, Rickards 14th, Bidgood 15th, and still the team chances looked rosy. Joe King had dropped a bit, Bert Field was 32nd and Alf 34th, but alas!
Our heartiest congratulations and very best wishes go to Joe Coleman, Bert Field and Jim Ginty upon their respective marriages. We wish them all years of health and happiness.
